title: Final Project: Mini Compiler
concept: Build a mini compiler for a tiny language using XIOM — applying all L7 concepts: lexing, parsing, type checking, and code generation.
why: Nothing teaches compilers like building one. This capstone integrates everything from L7 into a working compiler for a small arithmetic language.
tips: Operator precedence is the hard part of expression parsing — use the shunting-yard algorithm or precedence climbing
Start with a simple evaluator (no precedence), then add precedence handling
Test with known results — arithmetic expressions have deterministic answers
This project pattern (lex → parse → evaluate) appears in every compiler, interpreter, and DSL
common_mistakes: Ignoring operator precedence — '1 + 2 * 3' must evaluate to 7, not 9
Not handling parentheses — they override precedence
Assuming whitespace doesn't matter — trim tokens after lexing
Not testing edge cases: negative numbers, division by zero, empty input
